## Function Project Registry

The registry of projects in one JSON file, rewritten whole and atomically, and a JSON state blob per project.

Behaviour: Declares in registry/registry.go: `var ErrNotFound = errors.New("project not found")`, `var ErrExists = errors.New("project exists")`, `var ErrBadName = errors.New("bad project name")`, `var ErrNoState = errors.New("no state")`, `type Project struct { Name string `json:"name"`; Language string `json:"language"`; RepoURL string `json:"repo_url"`; Dir string `json:"dir"`; Caps queue.Caps `json:"caps"`; CreatedAt time.Time `json:"created_at"`; User string `json:"user,omitempty"` }` (User names the project's user of package users, "" = the operator's project), `type Registry struct { base string; projects []Project }` (unexported fields; registry/secrets.go reads r.base), `func Open(base string) (*Registry, error)`, `func (r *Registry) Base() string`, `func (r *Registry) Add(p Project) error`, `func (r *Registry) Get(name string) (Project, error)`, `func (r *Registry) List() []Project`, `func (r *Registry) ListUser(user string) []Project`, `func (r *Registry) SaveState(name string, v any) error` and `func (r *Registry) LoadState(name string, v any) error`. Open creates base (0o700) when missing and reads base/projects.json: missing → empty; not a JSON array of Project → (nil, an error beginning "registry: read "). Add: Name must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,39}$ else ErrBadName; a stored name → ErrExists; else stored and the whole list written as a JSON array sorted by Name (json.MarshalIndent with two spaces, an empty list as []) to a temporary file in base then renamed onto projects.json. Get → the project or (Project{}, ErrNotFound). List → a new slice sorted by Name (empty non-nil). ListUser → a new slice of the projects whose User equals user, sorted by Name (empty non-nil); ListUser("") is the operator's projects. A projects.json written before User existed (entries without the key "user") opens with User "" on every project; a project with User "" is written without the key "user". SaveState writes json.MarshalIndent(v) to base/<name>/state.json (the directory created 0o700; unknown name → ErrNotFound) by temporary file and rename; LoadState unmarshals it into v, missing file → ErrNoState, unknown name → ErrNotFound. Every error of the file system is returned as is (never one of the sentinels). Values are copies.

Steps:
- uses: queue
- produces: Project

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given base := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "state") (missing); when Open(base); List(); Get("demo"); Base(); then a non-nil *Registry, nil; the directory exists; []Project{} (non-nil, empty); (Project{}, ErrNotFound); base
2. given the registry of example 1; Add({Name "zeta", Language "go", RepoURL "https://github.com/o/zeta", Dir "/p/zeta", Caps {30, 3, 5}, CreatedAt 2026-10-08T15:00:00Z}); Add({Name "alpha", Language "python", …, CreatedAt 2026-10-08T15:01:00Z}); when Add twice, then List, then decode base/projects.json; then both nil; List names in order "alpha", "zeta"; the file decodes (json.Unmarshal into []Project) to exactly List(); the directory base holds only projects.json
3. given the registry after example 2; when Add({Name "alpha"}); Add({Name "Alpha"}); Add({Name "-x"}); Add({Name 41 × "a"}); then ErrExists; ErrBadName; ErrBadName; ErrBadName; List still 2
4. given the file written by example 2, Open(base) again; when List; Get("zeta"); then equal field by field to the first registry's List (times round-trip through JSON); Get returns the zeta project
5. given the registry after example 2; type S struct{ N int `json:"n"` }; when SaveState("alpha", S{7}); LoadState("alpha", &out); LoadState("zeta", &out2); SaveState("nope", S{1}); LoadState("nope", &out3); then nil; nil and out == S{7}; ErrNoState; ErrNotFound; ErrNotFound; base/alpha/state.json exists with mode & 0o777 == 0o600 and base/alpha mode & 0o777 == 0o700
6. given base/projects.json holding the text {not json; when Open; then (nil, an error beginning "registry: read ")
7. given the registry of example 1 after Add({Name "alpha", Language "go", Dir "/p/alpha"}); when p := List(); p[0].Name = "changed"; p = append(p, Project{Name: "extra"}); g, _ := Get("alpha"); g.Name = "changed"; then List() and Get("alpha"); then List() is exactly []Project{{Name: "alpha", Language: "go", Dir: "/p/alpha"}} and Get("alpha") returns that project, nil: writes to returned values never reach the registry
8. given base := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "state"); Open(base); Add({Name "alpha", Language "go", RepoURL "https://github.com/ann/alpha", Dir "/home/mu-ann/projects/alpha", Caps {30, 3, 5}, CreatedAt 2026-10-12T09:00:00Z, User "ann"}); Add({Name "beta", Language "python", RepoURL "https://github.com/bob/beta", Dir "/home/mu-bob/projects/beta", CreatedAt 2026-10-12T09:05:00Z, User "bob"}); Add({Name "core", Language "go", Dir "/home/morph/projects/core", CreatedAt 2026-10-12T09:10:00Z}); when ListUser("ann"); ListUser("bob"); ListUser(""); ListUser("eve"); List(); then l := ListUser("ann"); l[0].User = "bob"; ListUser("bob"); then []Project{alpha}; []Project{beta}; []Project{core}; []Project{} (non-nil, empty); names "alpha", "beta", "core"; still []Project{beta}: a write to a returned value never reaches the registry
9. given the registry of example 8; a second base whose projects.json holds the text [{"name":"old","dir":"/p/old"}]; when decode base/projects.json into []map[string]any; Open(base) again and Get("alpha"); Open(the second base) and Get("old"); then entry 0 has "user": "ann", entry 2 (core) has no key "user"; the alpha project of example 8 field by field, nil; (Project{Name: "old", Dir: "/p/old"}, nil) with User ""

## Component requirements / guardrails

Requirements:
- Claude Behind An Interface: The claude CLI is reached only through claude.Process (stdin lines in, stdout lines out, an exit status); the daemon's tests use claude.Fake fed with lines from tests/fixtures/stream/probe.jsonl, never a real claude.
- Bearer Token On Every Route: Every HTTP route but GET /healthz and the MCP endpoints requires Authorization: Bearer <MORPHD_TOKEN>; /mcp and /mcp/{project} require the same token; /mcp/{project}/session requires that project's current session token. morphd listens on 127.0.0.1 only; TLS and the public name are Caddy's.
- The Session Reports Only Itself: A VPS session can call phase_done, wait_operator and milestone only through its own endpoint /mcp/{project}/session with the token morphd minted for that spawn; the token changes on every spawn, so a past session or another project cannot report.

Guardrails:
- Injected Clock And Ids: No package but cmd/morphd reads the clock or a random source: time comes in as a `now` argument or an injected Now func() time.Time, ids from an injected NewID func() string; time.Now, math/rand and crypto/rand appear only in cmd/morphd. Timers are the daemon's Tick, driven by main's ticker.
- No Network In Tests: Tests never open a listener or dial: HTTP is tested with httptest.NewRecorder and httptest.NewRequest, Telegram and GitHub through an injected Do, the MCP server over in-memory transports; a test writes files only under t.TempDir(); no test runs claude or reaches github.com or api.telegram.org.
- No Shell Outside Runner: os/exec is imported only by package runner (git, morph) and package claude (the claude process); every other package runs commands through runner.Runner and tests script them with runner.Fake.
- Secrets Never Logged: The API token, the session tokens, the GitHub token and the Telegram token never appear in a response body, a log line, a milestone, an error text or the argv of a spawned process; secrets live in files of mode 0600 under the state directory; the git credentials reach git through a credential store file, never through a URL or an argument.

Write the files: `registry/registry.go`.

Go 1.22, the standard library only (go.mod requires nothing; the build runs with GOPROXY=off). gofmt-formatted (gofmt -l prints nothing) and go vet clean. A file's package is its directory's base name; exported names in MixedCaps; a package imports another of the module by the module path of go.mod + "/" + its directory. Tests are `func TestXxx(t *testing.T)` in the package's own `_test.go` files, table tests allowed; compare with `testhelp.Equal(t, what, got, want)` of the module's `internal/testhelp`, never your own helper; no t.Skip, no network, no clock, no goroutine left running.

## Function User Registry

The users of morphd in one JSON file, rewritten whole and atomically; a token is stored only as its SHA-256 hash.

Behaviour: Declares in users/users.go: `var ErrNotFound = errors.New("users: user not found")`, `var ErrExists = errors.New("users: user exists")`, `var ErrBadName = errors.New("users: bad user name")`, `var ErrChatTaken = errors.New("users: chat bound to another user")`, `var ErrEmptyToken = errors.New("users: empty token")`, `var ErrTokenTaken = errors.New("users: token taken")`, `type User struct { Name string `json:"name"`; LinuxUser string `json:"linux_user"`; ChatID int64 `json:"chat_id"`; TokenHash string `json:"token_hash"`; CreatedAt time.Time `json:"created_at"` }`, `type Registry struct { mu sync.Mutex; base string; users []User }` (unexported fields; users/secrets.go and users/tokens.go read r.base and r.users), `func HashToken(token string) string` = the lower-case hex of sha256.Sum256 of the token's bytes, `func Open(base string) (*Registry, error)`, `func (r *Registry) Base() string`, `func (r *Registry) Add(name string, now time.Time) (User, error)`, `func (r *Registry) Get(name string) (User, error)`, `func (r *Registry) List() []User`, `func (r *Registry) ByChat(chatID int64) (User, error)`, `func (r *Registry) SetChat(name string, chatID int64) error` and `func (r *Registry) SetToken(name, token string) error`. Every exported method holds r.mu for its whole body (Get, List and ByChat too). Open creates base (0o700) when missing and reads base/users.json: missing → empty; not a JSON array of User → (nil, an error beginning "users: read "). Add: name must match ^[a-z][a-z0-9]{0,15}$ else ErrBadName; a stored name → ErrExists; else User{Name: name, LinuxUser: "mu-" + name, CreatedAt: now} is stored and returned. SetChat: unknown name → ErrNotFound; chatID != 0 already the ChatID of another user → ErrChatTaken; else the user's ChatID = chatID (0 unbinds). SetToken: unknown name → ErrNotFound; token "" → ErrEmptyToken; HashToken(token) already the TokenHash of another user → ErrTokenTaken; else the user's TokenHash = HashToken(token); the token itself is never stored, returned or put into an error text. Every successful Add, SetChat and SetToken writes the whole list as a JSON array sorted by Name (json.MarshalIndent with two spaces, no trailing newline, an empty list as []) to a temporary file (mode 0o600) in base, renamed onto base/users.json; a failed call writes nothing. Get → the user or (User{}, ErrNotFound). List → a new slice sorted by Name (empty non-nil). ByChat: chatID 0 → (User{}, ErrNotFound); else the user whose ChatID equals it, or (User{}, ErrNotFound). Every error of the file system is returned as is. Values are copies. tests/fixtures/users/users-3.json is the exact users.json of three users: ann (ChatID 111111111, the token "mcp-ann-0001", created 2026-10-12T09:00:00Z), bob (ChatID 0, the token "mcp-bob-0002", created 2026-10-12T09:05:00Z) and eve (ChatID 333333333, no token, created 2026-10-12T09:10:00Z).

Steps:
- produces: User

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given base := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "users") (missing); when Open(base); List(); Get("ann"); ByChat(0); Base(); the texts of ErrNotFound, ErrExists, ErrBadName, ErrChatTaken, ErrEmptyToken, ErrTokenTaken; then a non-nil *Registry, nil; base exists with mode & 0o777 == 0o700; []User{} (non-nil, empty); (User{}, ErrNotFound); (User{}, ErrNotFound); base; "users: user not found", "users: user exists", "users: bad user name", "users: chat bound to another user", "users: empty token", "users: token taken"
2. given the registry of example 1; when Add("eve", 2026-10-12T09:10:00Z); Add("ann", 2026-10-12T09:00:00Z); Add("bob", 2026-10-12T09:05:00Z); SetChat("ann", 111111111); SetChat("eve", 333333333); SetToken("ann", "mcp-ann-0001"); SetToken("bob", "mcp-bob-0002"); then read base/users.json; then the first Add returns (User{Name: "eve", LinuxUser: "mu-eve", ChatID: 0, TokenHash: "", CreatedAt: 2026-10-12T09:10:00Z}, nil), the other calls nil; the bytes of base/users.json equal the bytes of tests/fixtures/users/users-3.json exactly; base/users.json mode & 0o777 == 0o600; the directory base holds only users.json
3. given base := t.TempDir(); base/users.json written with the bytes of tests/fixtures/users/users-3.json; Open(base); when List(); Get("bob"); ByChat(333333333); ByChat(222222222); then List is []User{{"ann", "mu-ann", 111111111, "44d5cbb64a5151b2608de24987b45d9344b8e60386c1a2d4f6ce8904f7e56d2b", 2026-10-12T09:00:00Z}, {"bob", "mu-bob", 0, "67cfcbd6b49e25979dbe31281596a0765b85aa0b22850cfbfc515247220055ff", 2026-10-12T09:05:00Z}, {"eve", "mu-eve", 333333333, "", 2026-10-12T09:10:00Z}}; (the bob User, nil); (the eve User, nil); (User{}, ErrNotFound)
4. given the registry of example 3; when t0 := 2026-10-12T10:00:00Z; Add("ann", t0); Add("Ann", t0); Add("mu-x", t0); Add("1a", t0); Add("", t0); Add(17 × "a", t0); SetChat("bob", 111111111); SetChat("zed", 5); SetToken("eve", ""); SetToken("eve", "mcp-ann-0001"); SetToken("zed", "mcp-zed-1"); then (User{}, ErrExists); (User{}, ErrBadName) for each of the next five; ErrChatTaken; ErrNotFound; ErrEmptyToken; ErrTokenTaken; ErrNotFound; the bytes of base/users.json still equal the fixture's; no error text contains "mcp-ann-0001" or "mcp-zed-1"
5. given the registry of example 3; when SetToken("eve", "mcp-new-0003"); HashToken("mcp-new-0003"); Get("eve"); read base/users.json; then nil; "866e38f9ff3bcf4eae882fcd6e81a2637709e9d6a7b5e6ec9fd7ec48ced9c413"; eve with TokenHash "866e38f9ff3bcf4eae882fcd6e81a2637709e9d6a7b5e6ec9fd7ec48ced9c413"; the file text contains "866e38f9ff3bcf4eae882fcd6e81a2637709e9d6a7b5e6ec9fd7ec48ced9c413" and does not contain "mcp-new-0003" (the token is stored only as its hash)
6. given the registry of example 3; when SetChat("ann", 0); ByChat(111111111); SetChat("bob", 111111111); ByChat(111111111); SetChat("bob", 111111111) again; Open(base) again and Get("bob"); then nil; (User{}, ErrNotFound); nil; the bob User with ChatID 111111111, nil; nil (binding a chat to its own user again is no error); the reopened bob has ChatID 111111111 and ann ChatID 0
7. given base := t.TempDir(); base/users.json holding the text {not json; when Open(base); then (nil, an error beginning "users: read ")
8. given the registry of example 3; when l := List(); l[0].Name = "changed"; l[0].TokenHash = ""; g, _ := Get("bob"); g.ChatID = 7; then List() and Get("bob"); then List() equals the List of example 3 and Get("bob") returns bob with ChatID 0, nil: writes to returned values never reach the registry

## Function Token Lookup

A bearer token to its caller — a user, or the operator's admin token that sees every project — by constant-time comparison of hashes.

Behaviour: Declares in users/tokens.go, over the Registry of users/users.go: `type Caller struct { User string; Admin bool }`, `func (c Caller) Sees(owner string) bool` and `func (r *Registry) Lookup(adminToken, bearer string) (Caller, bool)`. Lookup holds r.mu. bearer "" → (Caller{}, false). The hash h = HashToken(bearer); adminToken != "" and subtle.ConstantTimeCompare([]byte(h), []byte(HashToken(adminToken))) == 1 → (Caller{Admin: true}, true); else every user whose TokenHash is not "" is compared with subtle.ConstantTimeCompare([]byte(h), []byte(u.TokenHash)) and a match → (Caller{User: u.Name}, true); no match → (Caller{}, false). Tokens are compared only through their hashes (equal lengths), never with == on the token text. Sees: Admin → true; else User != "" and owner == User (a project with owner "" is the operator's: only the admin sees it).

Steps:
- calls: User Registry
- produces: Caller

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given base := t.TempDir(); base/users.json written with the bytes of tests/fixtures/users/users-3.json; r, _ := Open(base); when Lookup("mcp-admin-9", "mcp-ann-0001"); Lookup("mcp-admin-9", "mcp-bob-0002"); Lookup("mcp-admin-9", "mcp-admin-9"); then (Caller{User: "ann"}, true); (Caller{User: "bob"}, true); (Caller{Admin: true}, true)
2. given the registry of example 1; when Lookup("mcp-admin-9", ""); Lookup("mcp-admin-9", "mcp-ann-000"); Lookup("mcp-admin-9", "MCP-ANN-0001"); Lookup("mcp-admin-9", " mcp-ann-0001"); Lookup("mcp-admin-9", "44d5cbb64a5151b2608de24987b45d9344b8e60386c1a2d4f6ce8904f7e56d2b"); then (Caller{}, false) each (the stored hash is not a token)
3. given the registry of example 1; when Lookup("", ""); Lookup("", "mcp-ann-0001"); Lookup("", "mcp-admin-9"); then (Caller{}, false); (Caller{User: "ann"}, true); (Caller{}, false) (an empty admin token matches nothing)
4. given the registry of example 1; when SetToken("eve", "mcp-new-0003"); Lookup("mcp-admin-9", "mcp-new-0003"); SetToken("ann", "mcp-ann-0002"); Lookup("mcp-admin-9", "mcp-ann-0001"); Lookup("mcp-admin-9", "mcp-ann-0002"); then nil; (Caller{User: "eve"}, true); nil; (Caller{}, false) (the old token no longer works); (Caller{User: "ann"}, true)
5. given Caller{Admin: true}, Caller{User: "ann"}, Caller{}; when Sees("ann") and Sees("") on each; Caller{User: "ann"}.Sees("bob"); then true, true; true, false; false, false; false

Get → the user or (User{}, ErrNotFound). List → a new slice sorted by Name (empty non-nil). ByChat: chatID 0 → (User{}, ErrNotFound); else the user whose ChatID equals it, or (User{}, ErrNotFound). Every error of the file system is returned as is. Values are copies. tests/fixtures/users/users-3.json is the exact users.json of three users: ann (ChatID 111111111, the token "mcp-ann-0001", created 2026-10-12T09:00:00Z), bob (ChatID 0, the token "mcp-bob-0002", created 2026-10-12T09:05:00Z) and eve (ChatID 333333333, no token, created 2026-10-12T09:10:00Z).
